      "text": "\n\n\n**Yes, this makes perfect sense**, both logistically for the tournament and culturally for *osu!*. \n\nHere is a breakdown of why their conversation is completely accurate to the game and tournament formats:\n\n### 1. The Match Duration (Mercy_zero\u0027s point)\nMercy_zero is absolutely correct that either format will take **about an hour** unless it\u0027s a 6-0 or 7-0 stomp. \n*   An average *osu!* tournament map takes about 2.5 to 3.5 minutes.\n*   Factor in the ban phase, the 90-120 seconds teams get to pick a map, the time it takes to ready up in the multiplayer lobby, and potential tiebreakers. \n*   A Best of 11 going to 5-5 (11 maps played + 4 bans) or a Best of 13 going to 6-6 (13 maps played + 2 bans) will easily push the match past the 60-minute mark. \n\n### 2. The \"Lazer\" Meta (wuyiomokunrin\u0027s point)\nThe comment *\"dependent on underdogs not fucking it up, rather than top players trying to FC... its lazer after all\"* is incredibly accurate to the current state of *osu!lazer* tournaments.\n*   **Slider Accuracy:** Unlike *osu!stable*, *lazer* enforces strict accuracy on slider heads. If you hit a slider early or late, you drop accuracy (and score), whereas in *stable* it was an automatic 300 as long as you clicked inside the hit window. \n*   **Consistency over Spikes:** Because of the strictness of the *lazer* scoring system (and standardized tournament scoring in general), a player who simply survives and holds combo without missing (\"not fucking it up\") is often more valuable to the team\u0027s total score than a star player who tries to go for risky plays to get a Full Combo (FC) but ends up missing.
